title: Re-parent without loops
description:
Dropping a scene object onto another in the tree makes it a child of that object. Write

```cpp
bool isAncestor(const std::map<int, int>& parentOf, int ancestor, int node);
bool reparent(std::map<int, int>& parentOf, int node, int newParent);
```

`parentOf` maps every object to its parent; roots map to `-1`.

- `isAncestor(a, n)`: is `a` the parent of `n`, or its parent's parent, and so on up to the root? An object is not its own ancestor.
- `reparent(node, newParent)`: refuse (return `false`, change nothing) if `newParent` is `node` itself or a descendant of `node`, or if either is not in the map (except `newParent == -1`, which makes `node` a root). Otherwise set the parent and return `true`.
hints: `isAncestor` walks up from `node` through `parentOf` until it reaches -1, returning true if it meets `ancestor` on the way.
`reparent` refuses when `newParent == node` or `isAncestor(parentOf, node, newParent)` (that would make a loop); otherwise it sets `parentOf[node] = newParent`.
